name: Industrial Engineering Technician
description: Industrial engineering technicians make production work better — process and layout, quality data, lean methods and scheduling — beside industrial engineers rather than on the machines. ⚠ Median $66,120, and the highest bachelor's expectation of any technician occupation here: 53%.
credentialNote: ⚠ No licence governs this work, and the accreditation question is the usual one (engineering technology carries six years to a PE against four for engineering, s. 471.013). ⚠⚠ But the decisive fact on this path is hiring: **53% of O*NET's respondents said a BACHELOR'S degree is required and 29% an associate** — the sharpest split on this site. Treat the associate degree as a first step, confirm what it articulates into, and compare the industrial engineering degree directly. ⚠ The portable credentials here are **ASQ** quality certifications and the six sigma belts — ask a programme which ones its courses prepare you for.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET: apply engineering theory and principles to problems of industrial layout or manufacturing production, usually under the direction of engineering staff. The tasks are the improvement cycle — oversee or inspect production processes; develop or implement programs to address problems related to production, materials, safety or quality; test selected products at specified stages in the production process for performance characteristics; compile and evaluate statistical data to determine and maintain quality and reliability of products.

⚠ This is the technician job that is mostly about data and method rather than tools. If what you like is finding out why a line produces scrap on Tuesdays, this is the role; if what you like is fixing the machine that caused it, read industrial maintenance.

Projected need — and the degree expectation

O*NET, on federal projections: 74,600 employed (2024), growth “slower than average (1% to 2%)”, 6,300 openings a year, median wages $66,120 (2025).

⚠⚠ And the education split is the sharpest on this site: 53% of respondents said a BACHELOR'S degree is required, 29% an associate, 11% a master's. That is higher than the mechanical technician occupation and far higher than the trades. Treat the associate degree as a first step here, not a destination — confirm what it articulates into before you enrol, and look at the industrial engineering degree beside it.

⚠⚠ The courses are worth more than the programme's size suggests

Nineteen Florida institutions award in this family, which is respectable — but the individual courses reach further and are worth taking on their own account:

  • Introduction to Quality Assurance — 15 institutions. Measurement systems, sampling and documentation: the language of every regulated manufacturer.
  • Concepts of Lean and Six Sigma — 12 institutions. ⚠ Process-improvement vocabulary that travels into healthcare, logistics and services as readily as manufacturing, and is frequently what gets a technician promoted.
  • Manufacturing Processes and Materials — 12 institutions.
  • Industrial Safety — 20 institutions, the most widely carried course in the whole engineering technology family.

⚠ A student who cannot reach the full degree can still take quality, lean and safety at a college near them, and those three are what a plant will ask about.

Necessary skills

  • Statistics you can apply — sampling, control charts, capability. The core of the job, and the part most people underestimate.
  • Process mapping and layout: seeing a factory as a flow rather than a set of machines.
  • Quality systems — ISO-style documentation, corrective action, and the discipline of recording what was actually done.
  • Software: spreadsheets to a real standard, ERP or MES systems, and enough data-handling to answer a question without waiting for IT.
  • Persuasion. ⚠ An improvement nobody on the floor accepts does not happen — this role runs on the cooperation of people who do not report to you.

Advice

  • ⚠ Confirm the articulation to a bachelor's before enrolling. With over half of employers asking for one, this matters more here than anywhere else on the site.
  • Take quality and lean early — they are the most portable credentials in the programme and they are widely available.
  • Get inside a plant any way you can. Production experience makes an industrial technician credible in a way coursework cannot.
  • Florida's manufacturing is regional — aerospace and space suppliers, medical devices, food and beverage, building products, boats. Ask a programme which local employers hire its graduates.
  • If the data half appeals more than the factory, look at the data science path: the statistical work overlaps, and the labour market is larger.
